title: E-invoicing in the UAE: what real estate companies need ready before January 2027
summary: Does the UAE e-invoicing mandate apply to your property business? Here's how it affects your operations, your systems, and what to have ready by 2027.
body_markdown:
The latest UAE mandate says all invoices to businesses and government bodies must follow the PINT AE structure and be vetted by an accredited service provider.


Property businesses send out various invoices like a machine gun. So, seeing a sudden complicated condition can feel stressful. After all, no one's told you how it lands on the invoices you raise for rent, service, or recharges.


This blog covers how the mandate applies to your property business, which invoice types are affected, and what to have ready.


**Does the e-invoicing mandate apply to your property business?**


This mandate applies to businesses in every industry. You qualify for the new rules if you're VAT registered and issue invoices to businesses and government entities. If you're operating from a UAE free zone, your[VAT obligations may depend on your free zone status](https://www.alaan.com/blog/vat-for-free-zone-companies-in-uae) .


That said, things do get messy for property businesses. You're probably running two invoice streams, one to businesses and the other to people.


- The B2B invoice is for your commercial tenant and any business buyer or contractor, and the mandate applies to it.
- B2C billing is the invoice you send your residential tenant, which isn't bound by the mandate yet.


While[B2B VAT rules](https://www.alaan.com/blog/b2b-vat-rules-uae-guide) still apply, the property industry has different roles and billing habits. Let's see how the mandate lands based on who you are.


Who you are Does it apply? Why


Developers Yes You invoice contractors, suppliers, and business buyers, all of which count as B2B.


Landlords Often Commercial leases are in scope. Residential tenancies sit in B2C, so they're not, for now.


Property managers Yes Service charges and recharges usually go to an owners' association, a business entity, not a person


Owners' association managers Unusual OAs are typically invoiced as a single entity, which keeps most of that billing inside B2B.


Notice the theme? The mandate doesn't care what you call yourself, only who's on the other end of the invoice. Business address, you're in. Home address, not yet.


## Which of your property invoices are affected by the e-invoicing mandate?


Invoice type In scope? What changes


Rent invoices Depends on tenant Commercial tenants switch to structured e-invoices.
Residential tenants see no change yet


Service charges Yes Charges to an owners' association move to a structured format through your service provider.


Tenant recharges Depends on tenant Commercial recharges follow rent into scope.
Individual owner recharges stay as they are.


Commission invoices Yes Straightforward B2B, in scope from day one, no exceptions.


Supplier invoices received Yes Your accounts payable process needs to receive structured invoices, not just send them.


Most property businesses aren't just one role. A landlord managing suppliers is also sitting inside an owners' association.


That overlap means you're issuing half a dozen invoice types, and each falls a little differently in the e-invoicing mandate.


### Rent invoices


Invoices you send for rent to business tenants must be e-invoices. Rent and renewal invoices have a consistent volume, so a steady connection with your provider will save you a lot of grief.


### Tenant recharges


Recharges mean passing on utility, maintenance, or shared costs to whoever's paying them. Since this goes to both commercial and residential tenants, watch out and change just the commercial bills. Tag recharges by tenant type early, so the right invoices switch format without anyone sorting it manually later.


### Service charges


These charges are often billed to the owners' association and count as B2B. So the mandate applies, and it expects only structured e-invoices sent through your provider. Make sure your OA is registered as the entity receiving the invoice.


### Commission invoices


All commissions are paid to developers or agents. In the UAE, these transactions are always billed to a business. Since that means everything becomes e-invoices here, it's the easiest one to automate.


After the e-mandate kicks in, your suppliers will start sending revised e-invoices too. Make sure your accounting systems can open a structured e-invoice before a supplier raises the question. The right setup and[spend management tools](https://www.alaan.com/industries/real-estate) can also help you set up other financial workflows across your property business.


## How will the e-mandate affect billing direct consumers?


For probably the millionth time: B2C invoices aren't covered in the mandate yet. Less work now, sure, but not knowing what's coming isn't the best feeling either. Chances are, the mandate extends to B2C using the same phased approach, just once the current rollout proves itself.


Since individual tenant invoices are usually your highest volume, it's worth standardizing e-invoicing across both types now and early. Running separate commercial and residential setups will mean maintaining two processes for what's really one job. Plus, there'll be less rush and rebuilding when the rules do catch up.


That said, don't forget to loop in your customers and align the changes with them.


**Leave some buffer!** When trialling residential invoices, make sure your invoicing software supports quick field corrections. That way, you can fix small errors without holding up the entire billing run.


## What property businesses need to be e-invoicing ready and when?


Nearly all property businesses are affected by the e-mandate to some extent. Standardizing e-invoicing looks like a two-word phrase, but it takes a tonne of prep work to happen correctly as a process.


Let's list what your business needs, from registration to invoice restructuring.


1. **VAT registration:** Double-check if you're VAT registered, since that's what pulls you into the mandate in the first place. Confirm your status on EmaraTax before touching anything else.
2. **An accredited service provider:** Select and appoint one through EmaraTax. This is the connection that sends and receives your invoices. Your accounting software can't do this step on its own.
3. **Invoice data in the required format:** Rent rolls, service charges, and recharges all need to sit in structured PINT AE fields, not a description dropped into a free text box. This is usually the slowest part, since most portfolios carry years of data in whatever format a management platform exported it in.
4. **A tested connection before go-live:** Run invoices through your ASP's sandbox first, so mapping errors show up in a test file, not a real rent invoice going out to a tenant.


The Ministry of Finance has dedicated[UAE e-invoicing rules and a timeline](https://www.alaan.com/blog/uae-e-invoicing-compliance-preparation) to make sure the mandate doesn't break the systems it's meant to fix. There are two rollout phases, and which one you land in depends on revenue.


- **Phase 1: Go-live by 1 January 2027:** You'll fall in this bracket if you earn more than AED 50 million a year. Apart from the structured e-invoicing cutoff, you've got to appoint an accredited service provider by 30 October 2026.
- **Phase 2: Be ready by 1 July 2027:** Everyone under the AED 50 million mark rides in the second wave. You've also got until 31 March 2027 to appoint a service provider.


Both phases run the same drill, just on different clocks. So if you spot a property manager muttering into their coffee about deadlines, that's probably Phase 1 catching up with them.


## How do your management systems fit into e-invoicing?


Your accredited service provider (ASP) connects with the system issuing your invoice. This single connection keeps a single record trail, simplifies e-invoice exports, and avoids duplicate links.


Most property businesses run two separate systems, and how e-invoicing fits in shifts depending on which tool you're connecting.


- **Billing with the property management system (PMS):** Property software isn't designed for tax compliance. So verify if the PMS can export invoice data in PINT AE format and connect directly to your ASP. Before go-live, make sure it also syncs back to your accounting system automatically, so your books don't fall out of step.
- **Invoicing with the accounting system:** Most software handles structured invoice formats well, so the ASP connection depends on a clean pull of PMS data. That import should also follow a set schedule and set guardrails to spot or avoid mismatches.


While it isn't a new system, the mandate does need one clear, new connection. Weigh patching your current setup against migrating to the other, then close the loop on the system connections.


## What e-invoicing activities to sort out by the end of 2026?


For businesses in phase one, 2026 is all about going live with the e-invoicing mandate. Everyone else gets to start the prep work to meet the phase two deadlines of 2027.


To reach the same finish line, an[e-invoicing readiness check](https://www.alaan.com/e-invoicing-readiness-check) keeps you on pace.


**Tasks to get in place or out of the way:**


- Decide who owns this internally, whether it's finance, ops, or someone new.
- Loop in your bookkeeper or accountant now, since they'll be reconciling the final e-invoices.
- Set up the ASP connection with your invoicing system and[accounting automation](https://www.alaan.com/products/accounting-automation) for clean data flow between your PMS and ASP.
- Pull last quarter's invoices and check how much data is structured-format ready.
- Run one full invoice through your ASP's sandbox before a real one goes out.


Even with the 2027 runway, don't let it lull you. Closing out all setup activities will give you enough time for ASP onboarding and to stress-test the e-invoicing connection more.


**Check your phase, then your systems**


The e-invoicing mandate cuts down on chasing missing or mismatched invoices. Records get standardized and easier to reconcile. Applying that same structure to B2C billing early means less rework later.

## FAQs


### Is e-invoicing mandatory in the UAE for property companies?


Yes, if you're VAT registered and issue invoices to businesses or government entities. Property isn't exempted as a sector, so developers, landlords, and property managers all fall under the same rules as any other industry.


### Who is exempt from the UAE e-invoicing mandate?


Invoices to individual consumers, known as B2C, sit outside the mandate for now. For property businesses, that mainly covers residential tenancies, since billing a person renting their home isn't a business-to-business transaction yet.


### Do rent invoices need to be e-invoiced in the UAE?


Yes, but it depends on the tenant. Rent billed to a commercial tenant is B2B and falls within scope. Rent billed to someone renting a home is B2C and stays outside the mandate, at least for now.


### What is the deadline for UAE e-invoicing?


Businesses earning AED 50 million or more need structured e-invoicing live by 1 January 2027, with a service provider appointed by 30 October 2026. Everyone else follows on 1 July 2027, with a service provider deadline of 31 March 2027.
